source.title: Learning threshold neurons via the "edge of stability"
source.authors: Kwangjun Ahn; Sébastien Bubeck; Sinho Chewi; Yin Lee; Felipe Suarez; Yi Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own learning-rate experiments and analysis of training dynamics in a threshold-neuron ReLU model, bearing on the large-learning-rate version of the claim. It also reports CIFAR-10 dynamics, but does not measure training classification error.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper’s own threshold-neuron bias results, the full sparse-coding experiment, and reported CIFAR-10 bias results. Its CIFAR-10 experiments track bias, logits, and activations rather than training classification error; they do not test the zero-training-error claim directly. Background results cited from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper's own sharpness measurements and single-neuron convergence theorems bear on V5's full-batch edge-of-stability component. Figure 4 measures Hessian sharpness during GD, and Theorem 2 proves convergence with limiting sharpness near 2/η. The record overlooks these results when marking V5 entirely untested. Bias changes alone do not test V5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors explain a learning-rate phase transition for negative-bias threshold-neuron formation through a mean-model approximation, and also rigorously establish EoS dynamics and limiting sharpness for a single-neuron linear network. They leave an end-to-end analysis of learning the full sparse-coding task open.
record.recipe_differences: The principal theoretical analysis uses a single-neuron linear toy model and a mean-model approximation for a two-layer ReLU network, not the benchmark classification-error recipes in the claim versions. Experiments include sparse coding and binary or multiclass CIFAR-10 dynamics.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate changes whether the mean model learns a substantial negative bias; the reported CIFAR-10 dynamics also vary with learning rate. SGD CIFAR-10 plots are shown at batch sizes 100 and 1000, with text saying results are consistent across them.

fits_no_version.finding: Small-step mean-model training leaves bias near zero, whereas above-threshold steps produce a bias bounded away from zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning a negative threshold bias in the analyzed mean model has a learning-rate phase transition near 8π/d².

fits_no_version.finding: Larger learning rates promote negative biases in the simplified ReLU, full sparse-coding and CIFAR-10 experiments, with associated weight, logit or activation dynamics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large learning rates can promote threshold-neuron formation and sparser representations in these tested models.

record.peer_reviewed: 37th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2023)
record.problems: The detailed theory applies to a simplified single-neuron model and the mean-model approximation. The practical-model experiments are described as indicative and report bias, logits, activations, or test accuracy rather than training classification error. The CIFAR-10 plot values are figure-only in the supplied text, and CIFAR-10 is binarized for the full-batch experiment.
record.rows_left_out: No reported claim-relevant result rows were omitted. Results on mean bias, bias trajectories, logits, and activation are included as findings about the claim's subject, though they do not measure any listed version directly.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; corrupted labels; model-size, regularization and early-stopping comparisons.
Teacher-student spurious minima and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, and very deep plain or normalization-free residual training.
Comparative effects of initialization on learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.

The wide-network squared-loss catapult claim, its initial linearized stability limit and divergent higher-rate regime; divergence from below the initial threshold. The single-neuron theorem establishes convergence near the threshold through decreasing sharpness, rather than establishing progressive sharpening. The ReLU experiment reports EoS during an initial phase rather than a general long-time result.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparative Fixup performance.

missing.what: Hessian-sharpness trajectories for the simplified ReLU network at η=2/2000, 2/1500 and 2/1000; the authors explicitly identify EoS during the initial phase. Add separate sharpness rows, with observed state for that component.

Single-neuron GD convergence and limiting-sharpness bounds: below-threshold gradient-flow regime in Theorem 1 and near-2/η limiting sharpness in Theorem 2, including initialization, loss assumptions and the nonzero-iterate condition. These results are not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. The supplied text supports V5 verdicts through omitted results, while all existing rows remain unlinked. Neither negative bias nor output oscillation is a substitute for measuring sharpness.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, or tests with corrupted or random labels, model-size comparisons, or early stopping.
No teacher-student experiment measuring spurious minima or the effect of student width.
No comparison of plain and residual networks by training error, depth, or shortcut use.
No comparison of initializations for learning speed or trainable depth. He initialization is used in the full sparse-coding experiment, but initialization is not varied.

The paper studies large step sizes and edge-of-stability dynamics in simplified models, but does not test the version’s squared-loss stability-limit recovery claim, sharpness hovering during full-batch training, or divergence below the threshold.
No batch-normalization comparison or test of normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance.

relationships.condition: Full-batch GD on the simplified two-layer ReLU classification model during initial training
relationships.reason: Based on text missing from the rows: Figure 4 explicitly reports Hessian sharpness at the edge of stability for η=2/2000, 2/1500 and 2/1000 during the initial bias-learning phase; Figure 2 reports non-monotonic loss decrease. This supports the EoS component in this setting.
relationships.display_finding: Sharpness stayed at the edge of stability during initial bias learning at η = 2/2000, 2/1500 and 2/1000, while loss decreased nonmonotonically.

relationships.condition: Single-neuron linear network f(x,y)=ℓ(xy), with the stated EoS initialization and nonzero-iterate assumption
relationships.reason: Based on text missing from the rows: Theorem 2 proves convergence to a global minimizer with limiting sharpness between 2/η−O(η^(1/(β−1))) and 2/η. Figures 8–10 illustrate the threshold approach and bouncing dynamics.
relationships.display_finding: The model converges to a global minimizer with limiting sharpness between 2/η−O(η^(1/(β−1))) and 2/η, with experiments illustrating threshold approach and bouncing.
